rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords in Berkeley may not use coordinated pricing algorithms (software using competitor data) to set rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell or provide such software to Berkeley landlords. A tenant whose landlord uses such software can sue for injunctive relief, damages, civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)

coverage.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley; applies to landlords using, and vendors selling or licensing, coordinated pricing algorithms.

rules.exemptions: Excludes trade association reports publishing renter data in aggregated and anonymous form, and products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines.
rules.penalty: City Attorney civil action for damages, injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; tenant civil action for injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing City Attorney or tenant awarded reasonable attorney's fees and costs. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.quoted_span: B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the city of Berkeley.

notes: Ordinance No. 7,974-N.S. amends BMC ch. 13.63; section 13.63.070 sets the effective date as March 1, 2026, resolving the brief's open question on the ban's effective date. The captured text shows the June 24, 2025 vote to pass to print; final adoption is indicated as July 8, 2025 by the document header/URL. Any interaction with state law on algorithmic pricing is not addressed in this document.
